messages.content: You are the librarian of an automated numerical-analysis lab. You only ever cite documents from the list you are given, by their ids in square brackets; you never add documents, dates or results from memory. Answer with JSON only.

Scoreboard fast_transforms, section entries, entry:
{
 "id": "opcount-dft-n8",
 "best_known": 120,
 "status": "open",
 "source": "Cooley & Tukey, \"An algorithm for the machine calculation of complex Fourier series\", Math. Comp. 19 (1965); Yavne (1968); Duhamel & Hollmann, \"Split radix FFT algorithm\", Electron. Lett. 20 (1984); Johnson & Frigo, \"A modified split-radix FFT with fewer arithmetic operations\", IEEE Trans. Signal Process. 55 (2007).\n",
 "n": 8
}

Documents from the reading list (summaries written by the lab; cite only these):
1. [duhamel-hollmann-1984] 1984: Split radix FFT algorithm. The split-radix FFT combines a radix-2 split of the even samples with a radix-4 split of the odd samples and reaches the operation count 4 N log2 N - 6 N + 8, matching Yavne's count with a clear structure. Results: split-radix FFT with 4 N log2 N - 6 N + 8 real operations
2. [johnson-frigo-2007] 2007: A modified split-radix FFT with fewer arithmetic operations. Reduces the flop count of the split-radix FFT for the first time since 1968 to about (34/9) N log2 N by rescaling sub-transforms so that some twiddle multiplications become free. Results: a power-of-two FFT with about (34/9) N log2 N flops, the fewest known
3. [cooley-tukey-1965] 1965: An algorithm for the machine calculation of complex Fourier series. The fast Fourier transform: for N = r1 r2 ... rm the transform costs about N (r1 + ... + rm) operations, N log2 N for N a power of two, against N^2 for the direct sum, with the algorithm stated for general radix. Results: the DFT of length N costs O(N log N) operations when N is highly composite
4. [yavne-1968] 1968: An economical method for calculating the discrete Fourier transform. An algorithm for N a power of two with the lowest operation count known for over thirty years, 4 N log2 N - 6 N + 8 real additions and multiplications together, later recognized as the split-radix FFT. Results: a power-of-two DFT in 4 N log2 N - 6 N + 8 real operations
5. [van-loan-1992] 1992: Computational Frameworks for the Fast Fourier Transform. The FFT algorithms as factorizations of the DFT matrix into sparse butterfly and permutation factors, with flop counts: radix-2 costs 5 N log2 N flops with precomputed twiddle factors, radix-4 and split radix fewer. Results: radix-2 FFT costs 5 N log2 N flops; the DFT matrix factors into butterflies
6. [good-1958] 1958: The interaction algorithm and practical Fourier analysis. Computes Fourier coefficients for N with coprime factors by a multidimensional decomposition, reducing the number of operations below N^2; the prime-factor algorithm. Results: a factorization of the transform for N with coprime factors (prime-factor algorithm)

Is the entry's best known value, its stated source and its solved/open status consistent with these documents? Reply with JSON: {"verdict": "consistent" | "inconsistent" | "cannot verify", "reason": "...", "documents": ["id", ...], "suggested_change": "..." }. Say 'cannot verify' when the documents do not state the value; never confirm from memory.

response.text:
{
  "verdict": "inconsistent",
  "reason": "For N = 8 the cited literature gives lower operation counts than 120. Yavne (1968) and Duhamel & Hollmann (1984) (the split-radix result) give 4 N log2 N - 6 N + 8 real operations, which for N=8 evaluates to 56. Johnson & Frigo (2007) gives an improved count around (34/9) N log2 N ≈ 90.7 for N=8. Van Loan (1992) documents radix-2 costing 5 N log2 N = 120, but that is a higher count than the split-radix and modified split-radix results. Therefore the entry's best_known value 120 and its implied sourcing are not consistent with the documents, which record lower known counts.",
  "documents": [
    "yavne-1968",
    "duhamel-hollmann-1984",
    "johnson-frigo-2007",
    "van-loan-1992",
    "cooley-tukey-1965"
  ],
  "suggested_change": "Set best_known to 56 (the count 4 N log2 N - 6 N + 8 evaluated at N=8) and mark the entry as solved/closed with sources Yavne (1968) and Duhamel & Hollmann (1984); optionally note the Johnson & Frigo (2007) improved (but larger-for-N=8) flop estimate (~90.7) and that the radix-2 count 120 (van Loan 1992) is not the best-known."
